cards.problem: Closed accounts leave personal data spread across six services, and support cleans it up by hand.
cards.decision: Hard delete every row tied to the account, orders included, after a 30-day undo window.
constraints: Every service deletes through one shared job.
acceptance: After 30 days no table holds a row with the account id.
Undo within 30 days restores the account exactly.

evidence.summary: Personal data for one closed account was found in six services during the last audit.

delete.definition: Deleting an account removes every row tied to it, in every service, after a 30-day undo window.

undo window.definition: The 30 days during which a deleted account can be restored exactly.

cards.would_change_my_mind: A regulator or finance telling us some records must outlive the account.

teachbacks.problem: People who close their account still get our email, and support has to delete accounts manually.
teachbacks.decision: Ship a Delete account button that clears the person's personal data within a day and keeps their orders under an anonymous id.
constraints: Order history is kept for tax and refunds.
acceptance: No service shows a deleted person's name, email, or address.
The revenue report for last quarter does not change after a deletion.

evidence.summary: Last month support deleted 41 accounts manually.

delete.definition: Deleting an account removes the account.

personal data.definition: The name, email, phone, and addresses on someone's account.

teachbacks.would_change_my_mind: Legal deciding that order history is personal data we have to erase.

examples: Every order tied to the account is removed.
The person can no longer sign in.
non_examples: The person's email stays on a mailing list.
Their orders stay in the revenue report.

termverdicts.note: Keeping their orders keeps a trace of them, and that is not what I call delete.
